reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining OneCoin through recruitment-dependent bonuses, token purchases and mining-related packages, while presenting extraordinary earnings and token-growth claims such as "unlimited profits" and doubling earnings. It explicitly encourages viewers to recruit teammates, join quickly and contact a group through the linked signup page, rather than merely analyzing or warning about the scheme.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not treat every price increase as unqualified good news. It says that "an explosion in price at the beginning is not always good" and describes its longer-term figures as a prediction, including an "optimistic and conservative" view. The weekly earnings illustration also depends on members generating a stated amount and on the viewer being qualified. Those distinctions matter: the cited figures are scenarios within a presentation, not evidence that every viewer is promised the same result.

an explosion in price at the beginning is not always good!
here we have an optimistic and conservative prediction of what will happen to Hong Koe in one-year

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to teammates, two-member examples, tokens and "unlimited profits." Those passages establish what the presenter claims the plan can offer, but the two-member calculation is explicitly framed as an example with qualifications. Likewise, the existence of tokens in packages does not by itself establish that any particular viewer receives a guaranteed return. The presentation's own caution about an early price surge complicates a reading of every growth statement as a certainty.

an explosion in price at the beginning is not always good!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An example can be conditional and still function as a recruitment pitch. The presenter ties larger weekly figures to adding direct members, urges viewers not to waste time during a startup bonus period, and closes by directing interested viewers to contact the group. A caution about the pace of price growth does not qualify away those concrete invitations or the promoted earning mechanism.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the instructional structure of what is being shown. The presenter introduces this as a first Portuguese presentation intended to make the material accessible across languages. It moves through an explanation of what the coin is, then describes educational kits and material meant to teach cryptocurrency transactions, before walking through the compensation plan. The speaker also announces a later tutorial explaining the company's back office in detail. The disputed bonus figures appear within that explanation of how the system is represented to work; their presence does not, on its own, make every part of the presentation a promise to the viewer.

You will also learn what a cryptocurrency is, will have more options to predict prices to be able to buy low and sell high
see you next video, where I'll be doing a tutorial on the company's backups, explaining each detail.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats explanation of team bonuses and mining tokens as proof of solicitation. But explaining how packages, tokens and a compensation plan are described to operate is also consistent with an instructional presentation. The quoted "unlimited profits" language is promotional, yet that phrase alone does not establish that the educational material and operational walkthrough are incidental rather than part of the video's central subject.

where I'll be doing a tutorial on the company's backups, explaining each detail.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational framing does not account for the direct invitation to join. The presenter explains bonuses that increase with a member's organization, urges viewers to act before a timed bonus expires, and directs them to a group contact. The sampled end frame also displays a signup URL. Those are recruitment steps, not merely a neutral walkthrough of cryptocurrency concepts.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation identifies an ordinary product component: educational packages with interactive materials, alongside direct-sales compensation. It also describes tokens that members can exchange internally or use for mining space. That is a proposed bundle of products, access and rewards; the excerpts do not independently show a viewer handing over credentials, transferring funds to the speaker, or receiving a guaranteed cash payout. Even the net-bonus description separates a cash portion from a mandatory account. The question is what this video establishes, not whether the offered business would prove worthwhile.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening's examples show an advertised compensation structure, but they do not document an actual deposit, a completed withdrawal or a guaranteed payment to this viewer. The tokens are described as part of packages and as usable within an internal exchange. Those details permit a reading of the video as a sales presentation for packages and associated rewards, even if its projections deserve skepticism.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed transaction is not needed to identify what the video promotes. Its sales pitch expressly links cash bonuses to the volume from a smaller team leg and matching bonuses to successive generations. It also says package-linked tokens can buy mining space and urges viewers to contact the group. The educational packages do not erase the recruitment-dependent earning structure being offered.
